summary: This round's data swap put the site-wide footer quote into the No. 05 testimonial row, so /collaboration-opportunities/ now renders the identical B. Kettler, IHLA quote twice on one page.
evidence: The fix swapped wendy-j-ruud for b-kettler-ihla in testimonialsByRoute['/collaboration-opportunities/']. But b-kettler-ihla's quote is hard-coded in components/layout/Footer.tsx:82-85 ('Thanks for your thought-provoking presentations and making sure we all think differently about our industry.' / attribution="B. Kettler, IHLA"), so it renders in the footer on all 19 routes. MEASURED at 1440 with Playwright: two blockquote.dm-quote__body--wide elements with byte-identical text on /collaboration-opportunities/, one at y=5601 inside <main> (column 3 of the No. 05 three-up row) and one at y=7245 inside <footer>, on a 7618px page. Both carry the same byline 'B. KETTLER, IHLA' in the same italic serif treatment. Confirmed by eye on both screenshots (.playwright-mcp/qa5-coll-no05.png and .playwright-mcp/qa5-coll-footer.png). Rendered-text occurrence count of the quote string is 2 on this route and 1 on the other 18. The fix's own justification comment in content/testimonials.ts states the opposite premise: 'It was harvested for the old site's footer, and the `footer` key below still points at it; nothing else renders that key today, so this is the first route it appears on.' The section's two constraints are that all three came in after a live event and that none of them is one of the ten on /reviews/, which leaves the /keynote/ trio; restoring wendy-j-ruud (the round-4 state, and the trio the source page itself carried) satisfies both with no rendered string touched, at the cost of the 45-character cell that .dm-testimonials--3 was just changed to absorb. If the length curation is worth keeping, drop the hard-coded quote from Footer.tsx and drive the footer from testimonialsFor('footer') so the collision cannot recur, then either exclude b-kettler-ihla from the footer on this one route or leave the footer quote empty here. Either way, correct the false premise in the comment block in content/testimonials.ts.

He has spoken and consulted with the biggest names in Agriculture...'. DAMIAN_BIO at app/boasg/page.tsx:128-129 renders only the first sentence plus a rewritten second one. summary: One instance of the meta-copy class the orchestrator cleared by hand is still live in rendered output: a sentence that explains the site's own click-to-load video behaviour to the visitor.

Delete the final sentence only, leaving "Cheddar News booked Damian in April 2023 to talk about climate pressure and the global food supply. Here's the segment, in full." Nothing else on the route depends on it, the poster and play control already communicate that the video is click-to-start, and the <noscript> anchor keeps the segment reachable without JS. summary: The skip link's target <main id="main"> carries no tabindex="-1", so activating "Skip to content" moves the reading position only by virtue of Chrome's sequential-focus-navigation-starting-point behaviour, not by moving focus.
evidence: Rendered markup is identical on all 19 routes: `<main id="main" class="flex-1">` with no tabindex attribute (grep over the fetched HTML of every route returns exactly one distinct form). Driven in Chromium at 1440: first Tab focuses `A | Skip to content | href=#main`, which correctly animates into view at x=16 y=16 w=196 h=45 opacity 1. Pressing Enter sets location.hash to #main but leaves document.activeElement === BODY. The next Tab does land on the first in-main control (`A /contact-us/ "Check Your Event Date"`), so the link works as intended in Chromium. The gap is that focus itself is never placed on the target, which is the part user agents implement inconsistently. Not a regression from this round: none of the round-5 fixes touched app/layout.tsx or the skip link, and this markup predates them. Does not fail any of the 13 client checklist lines.
suggestedFix: Add tabindex="-1" to the <main id="main"> element in app/layout.tsx. One attribute, no CSS and no copy change; it makes the target programmatically focusable so activating the skip link moves real focus in every engine rather than relying on the starting-point heuristic. Pair it with `#main:focus { outline: none }` only if a focus ring on the whole main region is unwanted.

summary: In the closing "Get your date on the calendar" band, the CALL THE OFFICE plate overlaps the body paragraph and cuts words off the ends of two lines. Broken from 768 to about 835px, i.e. the whole tablet-portrait band (iPad 768, iPad 9th gen 810, iPad 10th gen 820, iPad Pro 11 in. 834).
evidence: Measured at 768: .dm-ctaband__body is x=32 w=397 (right edge 429) and .dm-ctaband__panel starts at x=414, so the plate sits 15px inside the text column and covers it for the plate's full 215px height. A site-wide grid/flex sibling-overlap sweep over all 19 routes at 390, 768 and 820 returned exactly one hit, this one: `dm-grid12 dm-ctaband__grid :: [BOOKING Get your date on the c] x [CALL THE OFFICE 888.304.0702] ov 15x215`. Confirmed by eye on a 2x viewport shot: line 1 reads "Email damianmasonoffice@gmail.com or call the offic" with the final letters buried under the plate, and line 2 reads "with the date, the city, and the room. You'll be talking t" with the same cut. Width sweep at 20px steps: 780 overlap 11px, 800 6px, 820 1px, 840 clear; below 768 the panel stacks and there is no overlap. Mechanism: `.dm-ctaband__panel { justify-self: end }` from 48rem (sections-core.css:571) plus a grid item's default min-width:auto, so the plate's min-content width (the 888.304.0702 numeral at display size, 322px, against a 5-of-12 track worth only ~274px) grows the plate leftward from the flush-right edge into the body column. Only this band trips it because every other plate's figure is short (14, 2,400+, 40,000+, 70,000+, 1994, 2020). NOT a regression from this round: cropping docs/qa/screenshots/round-4-mobile/06-meeting-coordinators-768.png at the same scroll offset shows the identical overlap, with the identical two words cut.
suggestedFix: Stop the plate exceeding its track instead of nudging the gap. Either add `min-inline-size: 0` to `.dm-ctaband__panel` and step the phone figure down one size below 64rem so its min-content fits the 5-column track, or keep the panel stacked under the body until 64rem the way it already stacks below 48rem. Re-verify by measuring body.right against panel.left at 768, 810, 820 and 834, not only at 1440.
